extracted.intended_audience: public company officers, compliance professionals, investors, law students, and legal researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how public companies must disclose material non-public information under SEC Regulation FD, including who is covered, timing rules for intentional vs. unintentional selective disclosures, and filing practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Public companies must disclose material non-public information which they shared with private individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation FD requires companies to disclose material non-public information that was shared privately (for example, advance information on earnings results). The rule is intended to ensure equal access to material disclosures for all investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intentional selective disclosure — simultaneous public release
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of intentional selective disclosures, the company must release the material information simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a company intentionally shares material non-public information with select persons, it must make that information public at the same time—i.e., simultaneous public disclosure to prevent selective advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unintentional selective disclosure — prompt public disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of unintentional selective disclosure, the company must publicly disclose the material information shortly afterwards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When disclosure to a select person occurs inadvertently, Regulation FD requires the company to publicly disclose the information promptly (the page states 'shortly afterwards'); companies commonly discharge this obligation via a public announcement or by filing a Form 8-K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing practice — Form 8-K
rubrics_metrics.description: Public companies file Regulation FD disclosures on a Form 8-K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulation FD disclosures are typically reported to the SEC through the Form 8-K filing vehicle, which notifies the market of certain material corporate events or disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — covered entities and recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation FD applies to public companies and addresses disclosures shared with private individuals such as securities analysts or selected institutional investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule was promulgated in response to reports that companies disclosed material non-public information to securities analysts and selected institutional investors; these kinds of selective private disclosures trigger the Reg FD obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and policy goal
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation FD aims to ensure that all investors have equal access to the company’s material disclosures at the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC adopted the rule to prevent unfair selective disclosures and to promote market fairness and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal authority / regulatory citation
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulatory text for Regulation FD is located in 17 C.F.R. Part 243.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to 17 C.F.R. Part 243 for the full regulatory language and details of the rule; the Wex entry notes this is the governing citation.
